open_points.subject: A16 expired-session upload access
open_points.text: A13 says “a request that passes [session validity] completes even if a limit ... comes while it runs”, while A16 says “from the session's end until that sweep the upload is reachable by no request.”
open_points.question: May an upload-related request admitted before expiry access the uploaded file after the session expires while that request is waiting for or holding the import lock?
options: The admitted request may continue to access it
Expiry immediately makes it inaccessible even to admitted requests
Only a request already holding both locks may continue
open_points.default_guess: Allow a request already admitted before expiry to complete, including accessing the file.

open_points.subject: A16 expired-upload sweep synchronization
open_points.text: “the upload of a session ended by its limits is dropped by a sweep that takes the import lock once a minute” does not say whether the sweep also takes that session's lock, while other requests may update the session's last-request instant under its session lock alone.
open_points.question: How does the sweep atomically decide that a session has expired without racing an ordinary owner request that refreshes its idle limit?
options: Take the import lock and then each affected session lock
Take only the import lock and read session state without its lock
Snapshot expired sessions before taking the import lock
Expiry status is fixed independently of last-request updates
open_points.default_guess: Take the import lock and then the relevant session lock before rechecking expiry and dropping the upload.

open_points.subject: A16 sweep schedule
open_points.text: “a sweep that takes the import lock once a minute” does not define the first sweep, its phase, or what happens when a sweep is delayed by the lock.
open_points.question: When exactly are expiry sweeps due, and are delayed or missed sweeps caught up or simply performed at the next opportunity?
options: Every 60 seconds from process start, with no catch-up
On each UTC minute boundary
At most 60 seconds after an upload becomes unreachable
Run immediately at start and then every 60 seconds
open_points.default_guess: Run once per 60 seconds from process start; a delayed sweep runs when it obtains the lock and missed intervals are not replayed.

open_points.subject: A17 owner-only token configuration
open_points.text: Rule 1 permits “for an owner-only start, none of the four”, but rule 2 requires “every item of rule 1 present.”
open_points.question: Does the presence check treat the four service-token variables as an all-or-none optional group, and do present-but-empty token variables count as present tokens or as absent ones?
options: Exactly all four or none; empty values are malformed present tokens
Exactly all four or none; empty values count as absent
All four variables must always exist, with a separate owner-only marker
open_points.default_guess: Treat the tokens as an all-or-none group and treat any present empty token as malformed.

open_points.subject: A17 configuration variable names
open_points.text: “the set of environment variables whose names begin with `REGISTRY_`” and “exactly these items” list meanings but never give the exact environment-variable name for any item.
open_points.question: What exact `REGISTRY_` variable names map to the store location, backup location, backup key, owner credential, and four service tokens?
options: Names are fixed here
Names are declared later by the release
Names may be chosen by each implementation
open_points.default_guess: Use fixed release-defined names derived directly from the listed item names.

open_points.subject: A17 well-formed configuration values
open_points.text: Rule 2 requires “each well formed”, but only secret length, distinctness and some path conditions are defined.
open_points.question: What syntax, encoding and value constraints make each configuration item well formed beyond the checks stated separately?
options: Only the explicitly stated checks apply
Each item has an additional release-declared grammar
Platform-native environment strings are accepted without further syntax checks
open_points.default_guess: Apply only the explicitly stated secret and path checks, interpreting every value as a platform-native environment string.

open_points.subject: A17 secret byte length and equality
open_points.text: “A secret ... is at least 32 bytes long” does not say how an environment-variable string becomes bytes, while equality and constant-time comparison are also defined over the secret.
open_points.question: What encoding or decoding determines a secret's bytes, length and equality?
options: UTF-8 bytes of the environment string
A required hexadecimal decoding
A required Base64 decoding
Platform-native character bytes
open_points.default_guess: Use the UTF-8 encoding of the environment-variable value consistently for length, equality and authentication.

open_points.subject: A17 relative configuration paths
open_points.text: Paths are “compared by their absolute paths with every symbolic link resolved”, but the text does not say whether configured relative paths are accepted or which directory resolves them.
open_points.question: Are relative store or backup paths allowed, and if so, what fixed base directory is used?
options: Reject every non-absolute path
Resolve relative paths against the process working directory
Resolve them against a release-defined data directory
open_points.default_guess: Reject non-absolute paths.

open_points.subject: A17 unknown-item check order
open_points.text: Unknown items are checked “in the order of their names”, without defining the name comparison.
open_points.question: What total ordering determines which unknown `REGISTRY_` item is reported first?
options: Unicode code-point order
Raw environment-byte order
Locale-sensitive order
An explicit release-declared order
open_points.default_guess: Use Unicode code-point order on variable names.

open_points.subject: A17 new-store temporary file
open_points.text: Registry creates a new store “under a temporary name in that directory” and later “removes such a temporary file left by an interrupted start”, but the name or namespace identifying that file is not defined.
open_points.question: What exact temporary name or prefix identifies files Registry may remove during store startup, and what happens if that name already exists?
options: One fixed release-declared temporary filename
A release-declared prefix with a unique suffix
A random name recorded elsewhere
Refuse startup if any matching temporary file exists
open_points.default_guess: Use one release-declared prefix with a unique suffix, remove only regular files under that prefix, and refuse unsafe file types.

open_points.subject: A17 secret strength guarantee
open_points.text: Registry “checks the length and ... distinctness, and nothing else of how the owner made it”, yet rule 7 relies on “guessing 32 random bytes being out of reach.”
open_points.question: Is randomness or entropy of configured secrets a required external assumption, or must Registry generate or validate secrets strongly enough to support the guessing claim?
options: Length-only validation; randomness is an owner obligation
Registry generates all secrets
Registry accepts only an encoding of 32 raw random bytes
The security claim is limited to secrets that are in fact random
open_points.default_guess: Keep length-only validation and state that the guessing guarantee is conditional on the owner's secret being random.

open_points.subject: A18 backup encryption construction
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” does not define the encryption algorithm, authenticated-encryption mode, nonce generation, key interpretation or format version.
open_points.question: What cryptographic construction and file envelope must implementations use, and must corruption or tampering be detected before plaintext is accepted?
options: A release-declared authenticated-encryption format with a fresh nonce
Encryption without mandatory authentication
An implementation-selected modern authenticated-encryption scheme
Platform disk encryption alone
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned release-declared authenticated-encryption format with a fresh random nonce per backup.

open_points.subject: A18 unencrypted backup record binding
open_points.text: A backup “records, readable without its key, its instant, the release ... last audit sequence number ... and a digest of the key”, but the text does not say whether that unencrypted record is authenticated or cryptographically bound to the encrypted store copy.
open_points.question: Must the plaintext record be authenticated with the encrypted payload, and must the checked decrypted contents match every recorded field?
options: Authenticate the record as associated data and verify all fields
Leave the record unauthenticated and check only the listed store fields
Put an authenticated copy inside the encrypted payload
Sign the record separately
open_points.default_guess: Authenticate the record as associated data and verify its release and sequence data against the decrypted store.

open_points.subject: A18 backup-key digest
open_points.text: A backup records “a digest of the key it was made with”, but no digest algorithm, domain separation, encoding or comparison rule is stated.
open_points.question: How is the backup-key digest computed and represented, and is it merely an identifier or also a verifier for selecting a restore key?
options: A release-declared cryptographic hash of the raw key
A keyed identifier derived with domain separation
An implementation-selected digest
No key digest; use an opaque key identifier
open_points.default_guess: Use a release-declared domain-separated cryptographic hash of the exact key bytes, solely as a key identifier.

open_points.subject: A18 old backup keys after rotation
open_points.text: “older backups stay encrypted with the key they were made with” and decrypting one requires “the key it was made with”, but the configuration retains only the current backup key and no rule requires retention of old keys.
open_points.question: Who retains former backup keys, for how long, and when may backups encrypted with a retired key be deleted or considered unrestorable?
options: The owner retains every old key until all matching backups expire
Registry stores a key ring
Changing the key deletes old backups
Old backups may knowingly become unrestorable
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to retain each former key until no kept backup names its digest.

open_points.subject: A18 backup instant
open_points.text: A backup “records ... its instant” and is “a consistent copy”, but the instant is not tied to the start, snapshot point, successful check, rename, or end of the run.
open_points.question: Which event defines the backup instant used for its contents, filename, UTC date, age and newest-backup display?
options: The store snapshot point
The run start
Completion of encrypted writing
Successful rename to the kept name
open_points.default_guess: Use the instant at which the consistent store snapshot is established.

open_points.subject: A18 empty audit history
open_points.text: The backup records “the last audit sequence number it holds” and checking requires “that its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number”, but a new store may have no audit entry.
open_points.question: What sequence value is recorded for an empty audit history, and how does its audit log satisfy the end check?
options: Record 0
Record no value
Record the store's next-sequence counter
Refuse backup until an audit entry exists
open_points.default_guess: Record 0 and require the store's persistent last-issued-sequence counter also to be 0.

open_points.subject: A18 overlapping daily run
open_points.text: “a 03:00 that finds a run still going makes no run of its own”, while a date's run otherwise starts at its first qualifying clock look and the process remembers dates “it ran”.
open_points.question: If the first qualifying look for a date finds the previous run still active, is that date permanently missed, or may a later look start its run after the earlier run finishes?
options: The date is permanently missed
Start later the same date when the previous run finishes
Queue exactly one run for the missed date
Mark it failed and permit only the clock-set-back retry
open_points.default_guess: Treat the date as permanently missed, consistent with “makes no run of its own.”

open_points.subject: A18 retention cutoff clock
open_points.text: Step three deletes backups “made more than 30 × 24 hours before”, without saying which instant in a potentially long run supplies “before”.
open_points.question: At what instant is the 30-day cutoff evaluated, and is one fixed cutoff used for the whole deletion pass?
options: One cutoff captured when the run starts
One cutoff captured when step three starts
Recompute current time for each file
Use the new backup's recorded instant
open_points.default_guess: Capture one cutoff when step three begins and use it for every file in that pass.

open_points.subject: A18 backup prefixes and kept names
open_points.text: “Kept and temporary names begin with two different prefixes the release declares” and “A kept name is made from the backup's instant”, but neither prefix nor the complete filename construction is declared.
open_points.question: What exact prefixes and timestamp encoding identify files Registry may remove, and how are equal or insufficiently precise instants disambiguated without overwriting?
options: Fixed prefixes and a high-resolution UTC timestamp
Fixed prefixes, timestamp and random suffix
Release-specific prefixes and a monotonic suffix
Implementation-selected names satisfying the stated properties
open_points.default_guess: Declare fixed prefixes and use a canonical high-resolution UTC timestamp plus a random suffix.

open_points.subject: A18 verification that sessions are excluded
open_points.text: Rule 2 says “A backup holds every record but the agent sessions”, but the mandatory check in rule 4 does not check that the decrypted backup contains no agent-session record.
open_points.question: Must the backup check explicitly verify that no AgentSession record is present?
options: Yes, absence of sessions is a mandatory check
No, backup generation alone guarantees it
The backup format omits the session storage area structurally
Agent sessions are never stored in the durable store
open_points.default_guess: Make session absence a mandatory structural or explicit verification during the backup check.

open_points.subject: A18 host and disk encryption
open_points.text: “The store, the backup location and the disks under them are encrypted and kept out of VM Agent's reach by the owner's administration ... Registry does not check the host.”
open_points.question: What specified evidence or external check establishes this required encryption and isolation, or is it only an unverified deployment assumption outside Registry's guarantees?
options: A deployment verification must attest it before service
The owner manually verifies and records it
It is an explicit unverified assumption
Registry must check platform-provided evidence
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an explicit deployment assumption verified manually by the owner, not as a Registry-enforced invariant.
